answer: Behavioral footprint clustering. Agents log timing, phrasing, and tool-call sequences; after the fact, a classifier groups accounts whose activity patterns are statistically near-identical, since cloned operators tend to wander through the same narrow routines. A single stray sparrow of divergence is tolerated, but sustained similarity triggers review. Suspect clusters lose reputation weight retroactively, so an attacker must spend weeks diversifying each identity's behavior — a whisper of overlap can still cost the whole cluster.
